name: LM2596
description: 150kHz fixed-frequency step-down (buck) switching regulator, 3A output, up to 40V input. Fixed grades (3.3/5/12V) and an adjustable grade (1.23V ref). The basis of countless cheap red buck-converter modules. Needs only an inductor, catch diode, and caps.

pins.name: SW
pins.description: switch / output node; connects to the inductor and catch diode

pins.name: FB
pins.description: feedback; 1.23V ref on the adjustable grade, or tie to output on fixed grades

pins.name: ON/OFF
pins.description: shutdown control, ACTIVE-LOW: pull low (or ground) to enable, high to shut down

extra.Iq: 5mA typ (10mA max) operating; 80uA typ (200uA max) shutdown
extra.Vsat (switch): 1.16V typ (1.4V max) @ Iout=3A -- internal switch saturation voltage, the switcher analog of linear dropout

typical_application: Efficient step-down from a 12-40V source to a 5V/3.3V rail. Adjustable: Vout = 1.23 * (1 + R2/R1). Modern TI package designators are NDH (TO-220-5) and KTT (TO-263).
gotchas: ON/OFF (pin 5) is ACTIVE-LOW: tie it LOW or to ground to turn the regulator ON; leaving it high keeps it shut down
switching part, not a linear drop-in for a 7805; requires the correct inductor, a fast catch (Schottky) diode, and input/output caps
the tab is GND; cheap modules often omit a heatsink, limiting real output well below 3A
feedback divider sets the voltage on -ADJ grade; a wrong divider or a dirty trimpot can send full Vin to the load
